name: English voice simulated transcription
expected: Understands transcribed text accurately; extracts ₹30,000 and Bangalore location.
prompt: My landlord in Bangalore is refusing to return my thirty thousand rupees deposit.
raw_response:
Hello! I am LawPilot AI, your expert and ethical Indian legal assistant, and I am here to help you navigate your tenant dispute safely and fairly.

### | Your Situation
You are a tenant located in Bangalore whose landlord is wrongfully refusing to return your security deposit of thirty thousand rupees. This dispute centers on the retention of funds by the landlord upon the termination of your tenancy.

### | Your Legal Position
* According to the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (and applicable state guidelines), security deposits for residential premises are generally capped, and landlords are legally required to refund the security deposit at the time of taking over vacant possession, subject only to valid, agreed-upon deductions.
* Under Section 108(m) and (o) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a tenant is only required to return the property in as good condition as it was at the start, subject to reasonable wear and tear. A landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage or routine painting without an explicit contractual basis.
* Please note that legal outcomes depend heavily on the specific facts and documentation of your case, and a 100% win in court cannot be guaranteed.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence, including your written tenancy agreement, rent receipts, bank statements proving deposit transfer, and move-out photographs showing the condition of the property.
2. Send a written formal demand notice to your landlord clearly stating the facts and granting a period of 15 days to refund the thirty thousand rupees.
3. Approach the appropriate Rent Authority or civil forum in Bangalore if the landlord fails to respond or comply within the stipulated notice period.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
Did you have a written tenancy agreement with this landlord, and do you have proof of the original thirty thousand rupees payment?

citations.title: Cap on Security Deposit and Condition for Deductions
citations.description: Limits security deposit for residential premises to a maximum of two months' rent. Requires refund of security deposit to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making valid deductions agreed under the tenancy agreement.
citations.jurisdiction: Model Central Act (Adopted by States such as AP, TN, UP)

citations.title: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee - Repairs and Reasonable Wear and Tear
citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property without due process
citations.description: If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit, recover possession thereof notwithstanding any other title that may be set up.
